label: <DEL> step, unless the first token (the first one to recall) is in {3,a,b,d,f,k,l,p,q,r,s}
explanation: 87% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (active on 51% of delimiter steps). Whether it fires there depends mostly on the first original token, which is the token output at that step: precision is 0.84-0.92 when the first token is 0/1/2, about 0.8 for h/j/z, and 0.10-0.36 when it is one of 3,a,b,d,f,k,l,p,q,r,s. Longer sequences raise the rate (L=9 delimiter steps fire even with first tokens from that set), and top activations are at <DEL> in L=8-9 sequences that start with a digit. The other ~12% of mass is weaker firing late in the original phase (t>=4, rising with t), mostly on first occurrences of the same disfavoured set (d,f,s,p,a,3,r,b,q,k,v); the predicate leaves this out. It almost never fires in the copy phase (0.2% of mass) or at t<3.
